Research software for computational conflict analysis. Everything is open
source; bug reports and contributions are welcome on GitHub.

::: {.software-feature}
::: {.software-hex}
[![](images/conflibertr-hex.png){fig-alt="conflibertR hex logo"}](software/conflibertr.qmd)

::: {.software-body}
[conflibertR]{.software-name}

An R package bringing [ConfliBERT](https://eventdata.utdallas.edu/), the
NSF-funded language model for political conflict and violence, to the R
ecosystem: entity recognition, event classification, question answering,
fine-tuning, model comparison, and active learning, all from R. On CRAN
as of July 2026.

[[Package page](software/conflibertr.qmd) [CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=conflibertR) [GitHub](https://github.com/shreyasmeher/conflibertR) [Cheatsheet (PDF)](software/conflibertR-cheatsheet.pdf) [Paper](https://doi.org/10.1017/pan.2025.10027)]{.pub-links}
:::
:::

::: {.pub-entry}
[NL Agent Explorer]{.pub-title}
[Interactive explorer of agent-level data on Dutch national politics, 2008 to 2025: every Tweede Kamer member and cabinet minister with offices held, party and parliamentary group, background, committee seats, bills sponsored with their Tweede Kamer topics and Raad van State advice, and a yearly stance on executive power estimated from plenary speech. Built for the TWIN4DEM project.]{.pub-meta}
[[Open the explorer](https://shreyasmeher.com/nl-agent-explorer/)]{.pub-links}
:::

::: {.pub-entry}
[ConfliBERT GUI]{.pub-title}
[Browser-based NLP toolkit for conflict and political violence text analysis: NER, classification, question answering, and LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning.]{.pub-meta}
[[GitHub](https://github.com/shreyasmeher/ConfliBERT-gui)]{.pub-links}
:::

## Fine-Tuned Language Models

Open-weight models for conflict and political text, all on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/shreyasmeher).

::: {.pub-entry}
[ConflLlama]{.pub-title}
[Llama 3 8B fine-tuned on the Global Terrorism Database for attack-type classification. Also available with a more neutral chat template and in four time-period variants.]{.pub-meta}
[[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/shreyasmeher/ConflLlama) [Paper](https://doi.org/10.1177/20531680251356282)]{.pub-links}
:::

::: {.pub-entry}
[ConflLlama-NER]{.pub-title}
[Llama 3.1 8B Instruct fine-tuned for named entity recognition in conflict event narratives: the source, target, and related actors of each event.]{.pub-meta}
[[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/shreyasmeher/ConflLlama-NER)]{.pub-links}
:::

::: {.pub-entry}
[ConflLlama-NER-TOI]{.pub-title}
[Named entity recognition for Indian news (locations, organisations, people, and time expressions), trained on 100,000 Times of India articles.]{.pub-meta}
[[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/shreyasmeher/ConflLlama-NER-TOI)]{.pub-links}
:::

::: {.pub-entry}
[Qwen-GLOCON-Reasoning]{.pub-title}
[Qwen2.5-3B trained with GRPO reinforcement learning to classify conflict events into five categories with structured reasoning.]{.pub-meta}
[[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/shreyasmeher/Qwen-GLOCON-Reasoning)]{.pub-links}
:::

::: {.pub-entry}
[Confli-mBERT]{.pub-title}
[ModernBERT fine-tuned on the Global Terrorism Database for conflict event classification; companion model to the paper on NLP model selection in computational social science.]{.pub-meta}
[[Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/shreyasmeher/Confli-mBERT)]{.pub-links}
:::
